i.e. when this watching has turned out best for me. The comparison is taken from the game of dice, where if you play with three dice, the best throw is to have thrown three sixes: hence the proverb ἢ τρὶς ἓξ ἢ τρεῖς κύβοι [either three sixes or three dice], on which see Zenob. 4, 23. Diogenian. 5, 4.

where the schol. says ὡς εἰ ἔφη τοῦ τρίτου κρατῆρος [as if he said of the third bowl], μετὰ Ἀγαμέμνονα τῶν δύο τούτων [after Agamemnon, of these two] (i.e. Clytaemnestra and Aegisthus) τὸ αἷμα [the blood]. Klausen rightly understands the first drink as the murder of Thyestes' children, the second as the murder of Agamemnon, the third as the murder of Clytaemnestra and Aegisthus, which Orestes accomplishes: an interpretation which Aeschylus' own words at the end of this play v. 1065-1074 supply.
